definition: Ideogram is a freemium text-to-image model developed by Ideogram, Inc.
details: using deep learning methodologies to generate digital images from natural language descriptions known as prompts. The model is capable of generating legible text in the images compared to other text-to-image models.

explainer.lead: Ideogram is a freemium text-to-image model from Ideogram, Inc. Its distinguishing trait is generating legible text inside images, where other text-to-image models often struggle.

tiers.eli5: It is an image-making AI that turns your written description into a picture, and it can spell words correctly inside the picture.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it with natural-language prompts to generate images that need readable text, such as posters or signage; a pitfall is assuming other text-to-image models will render text as legibly.
tiers.paperLevel: A freemium deep-learning text-to-image model that generates digital images from natural-language descriptions known as prompts and is capable of generating legible text in images. Known limits: the given facts do not state resolution, training data, or benchmark performance.

explainer.example: A user prompts for a poster design with a specific word on it, and the model renders that word legibly in the image.
